title: Body dispatch, flag validation, and mean node/apogee formulas
description:
Implement the core dispatch logic in src/calc.rs: flag validation, body routing, and mean node/apogee formulas.

## 1. `plaus_iflag()` (sweph.c:~200–308)

Flag validation and normalization. Key rules:
- Mutual exclusions: HELCTR+TOPOCTR → clear TOPOCTR. BARYCTR+TOPOCTR → clear TOPOCTR. HELCTR+BARYCTR → clear BARYCTR.
- Body restrictions: Moon/nodes can't be heliocentric (silently clear HELCTR). Earth only meaningful with HELCTR or BARYCTR.
- Default ephemeris: if none of JPLEPH/SWIEPH/MOSEPH set → add DEFAULTEPH (currently SWIEPH, but for Moshier-only phase, force MOSEPH).
- TRUEPOS implies NOABERR+NOGDEFL (set them if not already).
- SPEED: if neither SPEED nor SPEED3 set, add SPEED (always compute speed by default — matches C behavior).
- J2000 implies NONUT.
- ICRS implies J2000+NONUT.

## 2. `swecalc()` body dispatcher

Routes by Body enum variant:
| Body | Action |
|------|--------|
| EclipticNutation (−1) | Return obliquity (ε, sin ε, cos ε) + nutation (Δψ, Δε) in CalcResult.data. No corrections pipeline. |
| Sun | Moshier backend → app_pos_etc_sun |
| Moon | Moshier backend → app_pos_etc_moon |
| Mercury–Pluto | Moshier backend → app_pos_etc_plan |
| Earth | Return [0;6] for geocentric (Earth is the observer). Or heliocentric Earth if HELCTR. |
| MeanNode | swi_mean_node polynomial formula |
| MeanApogee | swi_mean_apog polynomial formula |
| TrueNode, OscuApogee, IntpApogee | Return Error::EphemerisNotAvailable (needs lunar_osc_elem, deferred) |
| Asteroid, Comet, Fictitious, PlanetMoon | Return Error::EphemerisNotAvailable (needs file backends, deferred) |
| Chiron, Pholus, Ceres, etc. | Return Error::EphemerisNotAvailable (needs file backends) |

The dispatcher needs to compute shared prerequisites once:
- Obliquity at J2000 (constant, could be precomputed)
- Obliquity at date
- Nutation at date
- Earth position (needed for aberration/deflection of all planets)

## 3. `swi_mean_node(jd: f64) -> [f64; 6]`

Mean longitude of Moon's ascending node, polynomial in T = (jd − J2000) / 36525:
- Extract exact coefficients from c-ref-calc.md
- Speed from two-point difference at NODE_CALC_INTV_MOSH (0.1 days)
- Output in ecliptic polar: [lon°, 0°, 1.0, speed_lon, 0, 0]

## 4. `swi_mean_apog(jd: f64) -> [f64; 6]`

Mean longitude of Moon's apogee (Black Moon Lilith), polynomial in T:
- Extract exact coefficients from c-ref-calc.md
- Speed from two-point difference at NODE_CALC_INTV_MOSH
- Add constant for mean distance if needed
- Output in ecliptic polar

## Constants to add
- `NODE_CALC_INTV: f64 = 0.0001` — node speed interval for file backends
- `NODE_CALC_INTV_MOSH: f64 = 0.1` — node speed interval for Moshier
- `NUT_SPEED_INTV: f64 = 0.0001` — nutation speed interval

C source reference: docs/c-ref-calc.md

swecalc routes all Moshier-supported bodies correctly
Unsupported bodies return appropriate Error variants

execution_record: Followed the implementation plan steps 1-9. Key divergence: the plan used `cotrans()` for the mean apogee inclination projection, but `cotrans` operates on degree-based polar coordinates — the correct function is `rotate_x()` which operates on cartesian. Also discovered and fixed a pre-existing bug in `precess_speed`: the C code uses obliquity of J2000 (oec2000) for the Date→J2000 direction, while our Rust used obliquity of date for both directions. This caused J2000 speed errors growing with epoch distance (up to 3e-7 at epoch -2000). All 165 golden test cases pass at 1e-10 tolerance. No other divergences from plan.

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex review: request changes.

Two high-severity findings verified against the codebase:

1. **ECL_NUT extraction path corruption** — `Body::EclipticNutation` stores [true_obliq, mean_obliq, nut_lon, nut_obliq, 0, 0] in a 24-element array and routes through `extract_output()`. This function treats slot 2 as a distance/radius (no RADIANS conversion), producing mixed-unit output with RADIANS flag. Also, EQUATORIAL reads from offset 12 (all zeros). C returns ECL_NUT values directly without any output conversion.

2. **Horizons flags survive MOSEPH forcing** — `plaus_iflag` forces MOSEPH but doesn't clear JPLHOR_APPROX / DPSIDEPS_1980. These flags are actively read in obliquity.rs (lines 24,37,67), nutation/mod.rs (lines 18,39), precession.rs (lines 83,605), and bias.rs (lines 43,94). A user passing JPLHOR_APPROX gets Horizons-adjusted obliquity/nutation/precession under Moshier — behavior C would not produce.

Neither is covered by the golden test cases (which test default/J2000/NONUT/EQUATORIAL/XYZ but not RADIANS or JPLHOR_APPROX).
